Confirmed the marker mismatch. Now I have what I need to write the design.

```gaos-design
---
task: wf-8-t-3
run: wf-8-t-3-a1
role: architect
---
# The design

Automated regression coverage for B06 — Teknis & Monitoring (his-vendor-backend), closing out
B06.01 (liveness), B06.02 (Swagger UI) and B06.03 (router 404/405 hygiene). The epic already has a
reviewed catalog (`docs/test-catalog/vendor-backend/system.md`, cluster `V-SYS`, 8 cases,
TC-VSYS-001..008) and three cases already have merged specs (`TC-VSYS-001`, `TC-VSYS-004`,
`TC-VSYS-006`, all `tests/api/rest/his-vendor-backend/TC-VSYS-NNN.spec.ts`). This design covers the
five still-`planned` cases (`TC-VSYS-002`, `-003`, `-005`, `-007`, `-008`) and a small refactor of the
REST client that the three existing specs should have used.

## What it does

1. **A typed probe surface on the existing vendor client**, so the `V-SYS` specs stop sending raw
   requests and start going through `src/api/rest/his-vendor-backend/his-vendor-backend.client.ts`
   like every other endpoint in the suite — closing a golden-rule-2 gap (`AGENTS.md` §2.2: "no raw
   `request.get()` ... in specs") that the first three merged `V-SYS` specs opened by calling
   `anonymousContext().get(url)` directly, because no client method existed yet for these
   infrastructure routes.
2. **Five new specs**, one file per case (matching the established `TC-VSYS-NNN.spec.ts` naming),
   each asserting exactly one behaviour from the catalog's Given/When/Then.
3. **One shared leak-marker helper**, because the two existing mechanisms for "the body must not leak
   internals" disagree today: the data-driven harness defaults (`src/data/vendor-cases/evaluate.ts`,
   `DEFAULT_FORBIDDEN = ['goroutine ', 'runtime error', 'panic:']`) and the hand-written
   `TC-VSYS-006` spec (`['goroutine', 'panic', 'sql:']`) use different lists. `V-SYS` specs are
   hand-written (not data-driven), but they should still assert the same canonical set the catalog's
   own scenario text names (`goroutine`, `panic`, `sql:`) plus the harness's `runtime error`, so a
   future reader does not have to guess which list is authoritative.
4. A documentation note (not an edit by this design) that the catalog and module-traceability rows
   for `TC-VSYS-004` and `TC-VSYS-006` are stale — the specs are merged to `main` but
   `docs/test-catalog/vendor-backend/system.md` still shows them `planned` with an empty `Spec`
   column, and `docs/modules/B-vendor.md` still shows B06.02 and B06.03 at 0% automated. This design
   does not touch those files (catalog rows are GAOS/engineer-owned, not architect-owned here), but
   the implementing engineer must sync them in the same change as `TC-VSYS-001`'s catalog fix did
   (commit `41a1209`), before or alongside landing the five new specs — otherwise the coverage number
   this product is scored against (BRD success metric) stays wrong even after the specs exist.

## How it works

### Client: `his-vendor-backend.client.ts`

Add a small "system" section to the existing `HisVendorBackendClient` (one client per service is
already the rule; these routes belong to the same service, just not to the omnichannel/VTT domain
surface):

```ts
/** GET/POST/DELETE /service-status — the liveness probe (V-SYS, B06.01/.03). */
serviceStatus(method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'DELETE' = 'GET'): Promise<APIResponse> {
  return method === 'GET' ? this.get('service-status')
    : method === 'POST' ? this.post('service-status')
    : this.delete('service-status');
}

/** GET /swagger/<relativePath> — the API documentation surface (V-SYS, B06.02). */
swagger(relativePath: string): Promise<APIResponse> {
  return this.get(`swagger/${relativePath.replace(/^\/+/, '')}`);
}

/** GET an arbitrary path with no domain surface — router-hygiene probes (V-SYS, B06.03). */
probeUnknownRoute(path: string): Promise<APIResponse> {
  return this.get(path.replace(/^\/+/, ''));
}
```

`BaseApiClient.url()` already joins `baseURL + '/' + path` and the registered base URL for
`his-vendor-backend` already ends in `/api/v1`, so these three methods reproduce exactly the routes
the three merged specs hit by hand (`.../api/v1/service-status`, `.../api/v1/swagger/index.html`,
`.../api/v1/thisisnotaroute`) without the ad-hoc base-URL string surgery those specs currently do.
`TC-VSYS-001`, `-004` and `-006` should be updated in the same change to call these methods via the
`vendorApi` fixture instead of `anonymousContext().get(...)`; this is a behaviour-preserving edit to
spec files, which `AGENTS.md` §6.3 lists under "may change freely" (no human approval needed), and it
must still pass 3× before merging.

### Shared helper: `src/utils/server-leak-markers.ts`

```ts
export const SERVER_LEAK_MARKERS = ['goroutine', 'panic', 'sql:', 'runtime error'] as const;

export function expectNoServerLeak(body: string): void {
  const haystack = body.toLowerCase();
  for (const marker of SERVER_LEAK_MARKERS) {
    expect(haystack, `response body must not contain "${marker}"`).not.toContain(marker);
  }
}
```

Used by every new `V-SYS` spec below in place of each spec re-declaring its own marker array.

### The five specs

All five are stateless GET/negative-method probes against public routes: no factory, no kit, no
`cleanup.add`, no seed — same as the three merged cases. All use `{ tag: [Tag.regression] }`
(matching the existing `V-SYS` specs; none is `@smoke` today, so none of the new ones introduces that
distinction unilaterally).

- **`TC-VSYS-002`** (B06.01, `+`, P1) — `tests/api/rest/his-vendor-backend/TC-VSYS-002.spec.ts`.
  `vendorApi.serviceStatus()` (GET); assert `response.status() === 200`, then `expectNoServerLeak`
  on the raw text body. Distinct behaviour from `TC-VSYS-001` (which asserts the `version`/`appName`
  contract) even though both call the same route — the catalog gives them separate ids and separate
  Given/When/Then, so they stay separate tests per the "one behaviour per test" rule rather than being
  folded into one.

- **`TC-VSYS-003`** (B06.03, `-`, P2) — `TC-VSYS-003.spec.ts`. `vendorApi.serviceStatus('POST')`;
  assert `response.status() === 405`; also run `expectNoServerLeak` on the body, because the source
  scenario (`SC-V-SYS-03`) states a 404/405 body containing `goroutine` or `panic` is itself a
  security finding, not just a status-code check.

- **`TC-VSYS-005`** (B06.02, `-`, P2) — `TC-VSYS-005.spec.ts`. `vendorApi.swagger('nonexistent-xyz.js')`;
  assert `response.status() === 404` and `expectNoServerLeak` on the body.

- **`TC-VSYS-007`** (B06.03, `-`, P2) — `TC-VSYS-007.spec.ts`. `vendorApi.serviceStatus('DELETE')`;
  assert `response.status() === 405` and `expectNoServerLeak`, mirroring `TC-VSYS-003` for a different
  verb on the same route (two cases, two files — the catalog keeps them distinct because the scenario
  lists both `POST` and `DELETE` as separate "wrong method" examples).

- **`TC-VSYS-008`** (B06.03, `-`, P1) — `TC-VSYS-008.spec.ts`, the path-traversal probe. Naively
  calling `vendorApi.probeUnknownRoute('../etc/passwd')` is unsafe to rely on: Playwright's request
  layer resolves the URL via standard dot-segment normalization before the bytes ever leave the
  client, so `/api/v1/../etc/passwd` collapses to `/etc/passwd` client-side — the server never sees a
  traversal attempt inside its own path space, and a 404 on that unrelated path would be a false
  pass. The design sends the dot-segment percent-encoded instead —
  `vendorApi.probeUnknownRoute('%2e%2e/etc/passwd')`, which normalization does not collapse — and,
  following the precedent already set by `TC-VSYS-006` (which asserts `response.url()` to prove the
  intended path was actually sent), first asserts `response.url()` contains `%2e%2e` to prove the
  literal traversal bytes reached the server before asserting on the response: `expect([400,
  404]).toContain(response.status())` and a body check that it contains neither a `/etc/passwd`-style
  path nor `expectNoServerLeak`'s markers. `expect([...]).toContain(...)` is an assertion over a fixed
  set, not a branch, so it does not trip the "no conditionals inside a test" rule.

### Catalog bookkeeping (engineer's follow-up, not part of this design's output)

For each of the five specs, the implementing change updates
`docs/test-catalog/vendor-backend/system.md` (`Done` ☑, `Status` → `automated`, `Spec` → the file
path) and regenerates `docs/modules/B-vendor.md` / `docs/modules/README.md` /
`docs/modules/traceability.md` / `docs/test-catalog/README.md` coverage tables with
`npm run catalog:report`, then `npm run catalog` to validate — the same sequence commit `41a1209`
used for `TC-VSYS-001`. The same pass should also pick up the still-stale rows for `TC-VSYS-004` and
`TC-VSYS-006`, since nothing in this epic currently credits their coverage.

## What it leaves open

- **Whether to migrate `TC-VSYS-001`/`-004`/`-006` to the new client methods in the same PR as the
  five new specs, or as a separate follow-up.** Bundling keeps the golden-rule-2 fix and the new
  coverage in one reviewable change; splitting keeps the new-coverage PR smaller. Either is
  consistent with policy; the engineer picks based on diff size.
- **The exact encoding Playwright actually transmits for `TC-VSYS-008`** depends on the Playwright/
  undici version pinned in this repo and must be verified empirically against the real staging host
  (assert `response.url()` first, as specified above) before the status/body assertions are trusted;
  if `%2e%2e` still gets decoded and collapsed by the client before send, an alternative is a raw
  `fetch`/socket probe outside Playwright's URL layer — not designed here because the simpler
  percent-encoded form is expected to work and should be tried first.
- **`/swagger/swagger.json`** is named in the B06.02 module-feature text ("Swagger UI `/swagger/*`
  (index.html, swagger.json)") but has no catalog test case; this design does not invent a new TC id
  for it — if the reviewer wants it covered, that is a catalog addition (GAOS-owned), not something
  this design or its engineer should add unilaterally.
- **An `Allow` header assertion on the two 405 cases** (`TC-VSYS-003`, `-007`) would be a reasonable
  extra contract check but is not named in the catalog's Given/When/Then; left out to avoid asserting
  behaviour the catalog does not ask for.
- **Running against production** is moot here (`config/env.ts` already blocks it); these specs target
  `TEST_ENV=staging` per `docs/vendor-backend-testing.md`'s existing preflight, same as the three
  merged cases.
```
